thread:
amy: :rotating_light: Seeing p99 spikes and streaming stalls for inference-path in us-west when feature-config fetches hit ~800ms, started at ~12:10 UTC. Customer-facing errors for a handful of large tenants, streaming sessions are stalling on token 2-4s tail.

devon: which dependency is spiking? DB or config service?

amy: traces point at control-plane config service: multiple `GET /v1/configs/tenant` returning 503/504 intermittently and a bunch of timeouts. Also seeing `auth` 429 bursts correlated with the same window. p95 for configfetch is ~120ms, p99 ~820ms over the last 3m.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20270303-001 — streaming stalls / configfetch latency. Paging oncall: @sre-oncall

sre-oncall: acknowledged — I'm on it. Quick question: is this limited to streaming route or also plain generation endpoints?

amy: mostly streaming (tail), but there are a few generation timeouts for long-context requests. Embeddings unaffected.

maria: adding logs from the control-plane proxy (snip):

```
2027-03-03T12:09:42Z proxy[controlplane] WARN upstream request timeout tenant=acme-corp route=/configs/tenant id=0x7f3c
2027-03-03T12:09:43Z auth[service] INFO rate_window_drop tenant=acme-corp allowed=10/60 dropped=45
```

lee: looks like a combination of config fetch latency and auth rate-window enforcement. If configfetch is slow, requests pile up and hit auth windows.

devon: can we short-circuit config fetch with cache for the streaming path? Maybe coalesce concurrent fetches so we don't hammer the backend.

amy: good idea. Short-term mitigation: 1) enable local cache fallback (serve last-seen config for 10s) 2) increase auth rate-window slightly for streaming routes 3) route new streaming sessions to a secondary control-plane region (us-west-2) if healthy.

sre-oncall: executing step 1 now — toggling `streaming.config.fallback_enabled = true` on edge proxies (rolling):

```
kubectl set env deploy/edge-proxy STREAMING_CONFIG_FALLBACK=true -n prod-edge
```

amy: on it. also pushing a quick patch to coalesce concurrent configfetch calls in the proxy (debounce 100ms). deploying canary to 3 pods.

maria: running curl check against control-plane config endpoint (sanity):

```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" "https://controlplane.us-west.internal/v1/configs/tenant?name=acme-corp"
# before: 200 0.78
# after: 200 0.09 (on canary)
```

lee: nice. I'm going to open a brief config service escalation to platform DB team — looks like index contention maybe during bursts. tagging infra-db.

devon: second mitigation: enable model-fallback policy for affected tenants so streaming can use a smaller kv-cache-friendly variant (lower token pressure). amy can you set that policy for the tenant group?

amy: applied `model_variant=fallback-small` for tenant group `acme-enterprise`. This will lower memory footprint and reduce KV pressure. :white_check_mark:

sre-oncall: auth team — please hold off emergency DB ops until we confirm coalesce/fallback effect for 10m. We may avoid a disruptive DB restart.

incident-bot: Note: customer impact flagged: partial streaming stalls for ~12 tenants, degraded latency p99 for those tenants. Status: mitigations in progress.

maria: dashboards now show p99 dropping from ~820ms to ~150-200ms for configfetch on canary path. Streaming stalls rate reduced by ~70% (observed from telemetry).

devon: timeline: keep coalesce enabled and fallback cache for 15m, then evaluate. If auth rate-window still being hit, we'll temporarily increase rate_window limits for streaming for affected tenant set.

lee: I've created ENG-DB ticket with traces and proposed index scan mitigation: https://jira.redwood/ENG-DB-5421 — cc infra-db oncall.

devon: also setting a short-lived traffic steer: route 30% of streaming sessions from us-west to us-west-2 until control-plane is healthy. Doing that via traffic-gate toggle.

amy: toggle done. Observability note: watch `streaming.session.stalls` and `configfetch.p99`.

sre-oncall: we should prepare a post-incident action list: a) persistent coalescing in proxy code b) client-side early-cache (ttl 1s) for critical flags c) revisit auth rate-window sizing per tenant burst profile d) run DB index tuning job.

maria: agree. Also recommend adding an automated fallback that serves a minimal config blob if control-plane returns 5xx for <500ms windows to avoid stalls.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations effective. Customer impact reduced. Next: schedule RCA and follow-up actions. Incident status: monitoring -> partial mitigation.

lee: handing off to oncall coverage for next shift: @sre-oncall will continue monitoring and coordinate with infra-db.

sre-oncall: oncall acked — I'll follow through with infra-db and update the ticket. Will publish a short postmortem once root cause confirmed.

amy: summary for postmortem draft: root cause likely concurrent configfetch storms + auth rate-window drop + under-provisioned DB index/cache leading to ~p99 spikes and streaming stalls. Immediate fixes: cache fallback, coalescing, traffic steering, model fallback. Long-term: proxy coalesce baked in, auth window tuning, DB index improvements, add circuit-breaker for configfetch.

devon: thanks everyone. I'll keep the canary until end of shift, then we can roll out more broadly if metrics stay stable.

maria: leaving logs and metrics links in the ticket: dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/streaming-incidents/2178004321

sre-oncall: closing the active paging loop. Will update incident ticket with timeline and owners for the action items.

amy: :thumbsup: good work — reduced customer impact without a restart. Follow-up owners: amy (proxy coalesce PR), lee (DB ticket), devon (traffic gate policy), maria (dashboards + runbooks).
